Apple regularly introduces new features for Apple Wallet, and future upgrades may revolve around trade-ins. Code also indicates that Apple may extend the validity period of trade-in quotes from 14 days to 90 days.

Apple Wallet adds new features

MacRumors discovered code referencing this new system within Apple's Guide application. For readers unfamiliar with it, the report notes that Guide is an application "used by Apple employees, Apple authorised resellers, and other sales organisations when talking to and demonstrating products to customers."

Within the Guide application's code are several strings mentioning the ability to store trade-in offers in the Wallet app:

  • "You can add this trade-in offer to your Apple Wallet. It will be valid for 90 days."
  • "To save this offer, simply scan the QR code with your iPhone's camera."

The exact implementation of this feature remains unclear. For example, the code mentions that trade-in offers can be stored for 90 days. Currently, Apple's trade-in quote validity is 14 days. It is possible that Apple plans to extend this period when rolling out this feature.

Today's report also mentions that a framework called "TradeInKit" is referenced within the Apple Guide application. According to the report, these new features are controlled server-side, and the relevant toggles have not yet been activated.

Apple raised trade-in values for most iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch models last week. Against a backdrop of continually rising prices, trade-ins have become an increasingly important part of the Apple shopping experience.
